description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05) by the Part B item B4 census (#1172).
PRE-EXISTING.  Not a wrong answer — a HOLE in the IR's declared vocabulary.

THE FINDING.  `docs/ir-op-inventory.tsv` (#1170) is generated from the
runtime's EXPORT list, and ir-spec §10 says the export list IS the inventory.
That is not true today: the emitter writes five names package-QUALIFIED, which
makes them work without being exported, and so they never appear in the port
list a backend author reads.

    pcl::%pcl-to-integer        `use integer`'s arithmetic (Pl/ExprToCL.pm:1602)
    pcl::%pcl-super-indirect    a SUPER:: call (perl-tests/method.t:1578)
    pcl::%pcl-local-errno-init  `local $!` (perl-tests/bless.t:303)
    pcl::%pcl-loop-tag          every labelled loop's catch tag
    pcl::p-qr                   every `qr//` literal (Pl/ExprToCL.pm:702, 1160)

The census found the first three the moment it stopped treating a
`pcl::`-qualified token as "a package-qualified program name" — which is what
had been hiding the whole class (a `pcl::` token is now legal only when the
name it qualifies is an export; tools/ir-host-leak.pl `_is_ident`).

`%p-empty-list` is the mirror-image case and is NOT one of these: ir-spec §10's
regex row cites it as the spelling of the empty list, but it is never emitted —
it is a runtime-internal helper, and the citation misleads a reader the other
way.  #1170's inventory reports both classes apart, under "Citations in
ir-spec §10 that are not IR names".

WHY IT MATTERS.  §10a's whole claim is "this TSV is the port list".  Five
names outside it means a backend that implements every row still cannot load
`use integer`, `SUPER::`, `local $!`, a labelled loop, or a `qr//`.

THE FIX, one of two, and the choice is the task:
  (a) EXPORT them, so the export list is the vocabulary again.  Cheapest, and
      it makes the inventory complete by construction — but it widens the
      runtime's public surface for names that are genuinely internal.
  (b) Have the inventory ALSO list the internals the emitter emits, marked as
      such.  Keeps the export list honest, but needs the emitter to declare
      what it emits — there is no list today, which is why the census had to
      find them.
(a) is the smaller change; (b) is the one that cannot drift, because it makes
the emitter say what it uses.  Either way `%pcl-loop-tag` and `p-qr` stop
being hard-coded exceptions in tools/ir-host-leak.pl.

BAR: `tools/ir-host-leak.pl` needs no per-name exception; the regenerated
`docs/ir-op-inventory.tsv` has a row for each; `Pl/t/ir-inventory-01.t` and
`Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t` green (the `useinteger` fixture's expected set loses
`op:pcl::%pcl-to-integer`); the gate; the full sweep if `cl/**` changed.

=== DONE (s470bo) â option (a), EXPORT them ===

All five names are exports now: `%pcl-to-integer`, `%pcl-super-indirect`,
`%pcl-local-errno-init`, `%pcl-loop-tag`, `p-qr`.

WHY (a) AND NOT (b): not because it is smaller (it is) but because it cannot
DRIFT.  `tools/ir-inventory.pl` reads the export list, so a future
qualified emission is either an export and appears in the port list, or is not
and shows up as a LEAK in `tools/ir-host-leak.pl`.  Option (b) â a second
hand-kept list of "internals the emitter emits" â would have had to be
maintained by whoever forgot the first time.

Nothing about the EMISSION changed: the emitter keeps writing them
`pcl::`-qualified, and no name gains a new meaning.  The five are filed in the
family each actually belongs to rather than left to the generator's sigil
heuristic, which read `%pcl-â¦` as a perl HASH and put three of them in
`magic-global`:

    %pcl-to-integer       bitwise          (it is `use integer`'s coercion)
    %pcl-loop-tag         control-flow
    %pcl-local-errno-init dynamic-scope
    %pcl-super-indirect   oo
    p-qr                  compiled-regex

`tools/ir-host-leak.pl`'s hard-coded exception for `p-qr` and `%pcl-loop-tag`
is DELETED with them â a per-name exception in the census is exactly what hid
this class.

BARS: inventory regenerated, **0 UNCLASSIFIED** families (was 1, the `p-qr`
row); `Pl/t/ir-inventory-01.t` and `Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t` green, the
latter's `useinteger` fixture having lost `op:pcl::%pcl-to-integer` from its
blessed set with the reason in the row's `why`.  Leak census over the 111
perl-tests files **41 -> 38 distinct**, the three that left being exactly
`%pcl-to-integer`, `%pcl-super-indirect`, `%pcl-local-errno-init` (the other
two were never counted â they were the exception).  ir-spec Â§11b's row for
this class is struck through with the closing note.  Gate 208/7035, only the
13 pclxs xs rows.
subject: FIVE runtime internals are EMITTED into generated code package-qualified and are therefore invisible to the op inventory a backend author works from
